summary: Windows 11 fast-user-switching breaks credential cache after depot reimage causing intermittent login failures
summary_details: Multiple users report that after depot reimage and standard post-image configuration the workstation intermittently rejects credentials when using Fast User Switching (Switch user) and shows a brief spinning 'Signing in' state followed by an error: 'We can't sign you in with this credential. Please try again.'
description: Issue summary: After depot reimage using the standard Windows 11 corporate image (build 22H2 + security baseline), affected devices intermittently fail to authenticate when using Fast User Switching (Switch user) between existing local/hybrid accounts. Impact: prevents quick user switching workflows, forces full sign-out or reboot, and results in repeated helpdesk tickets. Suspected link to credential manager or LSA cache not being reseeded after image + post-provision tasks.
impact: Approximately 12 devices in the last 48 hours across two teams; impacts developer and support engineers who rely on fast user switching for quick context changes. Workarounds are disruptive (full sign-out) and not acceptable for on-call rotation.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy corporate image via depot reimage workflow and apply Intune device config + SSO profiles.
2) Log in as AzureAD-hybrid account (user A).
3) Use 'Switch user' and log in as local or another AzureAD-hybrid account (user B).
4) Attempt to switch back to user A using cached credential or PIN.
5) Observe 'We can't sign you in with this credential' or immediate sign-in failure; only full sign-out or reboot restores switch behavior.
observed_behavior: Intermittent credential rejection on switch; event viewer shows 'LSA: Cred cache lookup failed' entries and short-lived NTLM/Negotiate failures. Not always reproducible on lab devices but consistent on affected fleet units after depot imaging with same post-image task sequence.
expected_behavior: Fast User Switching should reuse the cached credential store or allow immediate PIN/Windows Hello sign-in without requiring a full sign-out after an image and post-provision configuration.
logs:
Event Viewer excerpts (System & Security):
- Security 4771: Kerberos pre-auth failed: uid=...; client time skew not observed.
- System: LsaSrv (EventID 1202): Credential validation cache miss for account 'CORP\\a.patel'.
- Microsoft-Windows-UserProfilesService 1530: Windows detected your shell registry file is not in your profile.
- Intune Management Extension: Policy applied: com.redwood.sso.profile v12.
Additional collected traces: netlogon.log (auth hops) and LSA logs attached to ticket (S3 link placeholder).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-05 10:14 - Triage: Confirmed pattern after depot reimage tasks that include SSO policy application and CredentialProvider enrollment.

2026-03-05 14:02 - Lab repro attempt: Reimaged 3 lab units with identical sequence; reproduced on 1/3 devices. Difference: repro devices had post-image script that re-registered a custom SSO CP provider (vendor plugin v3.2).

2026-03-06 09:31 - Hypothesis A: Custom Cred Provider registration ordering race with LSA service leading to partially-initialized credential cache.
Hypothesis B: Intune SSO profile overwrites or delays PIN/Hello registration causing credential metadata mismatch.

2026-03-07 11:22 - Captured process dump of lsass.exe during repro; observed small delay in call sequence CreateCredential/CacheWrite; vendor CP returned STATUS_NOT_READY then worked on subsequent calls.
2026-03-08 15:45 - Correlation: All repros used CP vendor plugin v3.2. Devices that succeeded either had vendor v3.1 or were missing the CP entirely.
2026-03-09 09:05 - Eng request: Capture full boot trace + registry hives for a repro device; SRE to coordinate secure upload.

2026-03-09 12:10 - Workaround identified: Disabling Fast User Switching policy (via Group Policy) prevents immediate failures; also a temporary fix is to force reinitialization of the CredCache by running 'regsvr32 /u <vendorcp.dll> && regsvr32 <vendorcp.dll>' followed by restart of LSA service (recommended during off-hours only).
root_cause: Race condition between vendor credential provider registration (vendor CP v3.2) and LSA credential cache initialization during post-image provisioning. The vendor CP returns transient STATUS_NOT_READY for early calls which the OS treats as failed credential lookup for Fast User Switching flows.
short_term_fix: Roll back vendor CP on affected machines to v3.1 via Intune Win32 app uninstall/install; push hotfix policy to disable Fast User Switching on the affected ADOU for remainder of the week.
long_term_fix: Coordinate with vendor to release CP v3.2.1 that defers registration until LSA ready or returns a graceful retryable response. Add post-image orchestrator step to ensure LSA is ready before registering third-party credential providers. Update corporate image baseline to include vetted CP version.
resolution: In progress: vendor agreed to hotfix v3.2.1 candidate. Rolling rollback to v3.1 for the 12 known devices completed 2026-03-09 18:00 PST. Policy to disable Fast User Switching applied to affected OUs as temporary mitigation.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-09: Deployed rollback package via Intune to 12 devices; 11/12 reported restored behaviour. One device required manual regsvr32 + LSA restart. Vendor provided pre-release v3.2.1 on 2026-03-10 for testing. Follow-ups: add post-image verification step to automated depot workflow (Jenkins job) to validate Fast User Switching on imaged devices.
next_steps: If green, schedule v3.2.1 rollout with canary (10% fleet) and verify telemetry for 48h
Add LSA readiness check to depot post-image TaskSeq by 2026-03-16
Create KB for helpdesk: 'Fast User Switching fails after depot reimage' with temporary remedial commands
